answer: To resist sybil attacks, each agent must lock a sequential memory-hard proof chain bound to a unique non-transferable dune of local compute. For every hollow identity an attacker spins up, they must recompute a growing working set that cannot be shared or parallelized across clones. The cost scales super-linearly with the number of fable identities because each requires its own live sequential state; a farm of 100 clones pays roughly the square of the cost of one, rendering large-scale fabrication uneconomical under capital and time constraints.
